archetype.name: Rebuilding (defense-first youth)
archetype.definition: A young Utah roster still rebuilding after seasons near the bottom, where the defense has taken a real step but the offense has fallen away and the wins have not come.

report.headline: A better defense undone by a broken, shorthanded offense: 1-9 is mostly earned.
report.take:
Utah is 1-9, last in the Northwest, 27th on the site, with a Net Rtg of -11.6 that ranks 26th. Nothing in the margin points to bad luck. The W vs Pt Diff is -1, and the differential implies 2 wins rather than 1. Two of the losses, to San Antonio and New Orleans, went to overtime, but the last five games were all double-digit-style defeats at a -15.6 average. This is a team losing because it is outplayed, and lately it has been outplayed by more.

The surprise is which end is failing. For three straight years the Jazz defense ranked 29th or 30th, and last season it allowed a 122.3 DRtg with opponents shooting 71.4% at the rim. This year the DRtg is 116.0 (24th), Opp Rim FG % is down to 64.0, and the 74.5 DRB % ranks 7th. That is still below average, 2.6 points worse than the league, but it is a real structural gain. The offense is what collapsed: a 104.4 ORtg ranks 29th and sits 9 points under the league. Utah is 28th in eFG % at 49.5, 26th in 3P % at 32.1, and 25th in TOV % at 15.0. Last year's offense was 114.1 and ranked 22nd, so this is a new hole, not an old one.

Part of that hole is who has been available. Lauri Markkanen, the team's most efficient high-volume scorer (56.7 TS %, 29 threes in 8 games), is listed Out. So is Jaren Jackson Jr., who has played only 4 games. Keyonte George, who carries a 29.3 USG %, is day-to-day. Without them, the offense has leaned on Darryn Peterson (51.3 TS %) and Ace Bailey (51.3 TS %), plus a bench that has been unplayable: Svi Mykhailiuk at 33.8 TS % and Isaiah Collier with no threes. The encouraging read is that Peterson (+6.8) and Bailey (+7.0) are the two best On-Off marks among the rotation regulars. The young core is not the reason Utah is losing.

Where this goes depends on health. The defense looks real enough to keep games closer than last season's 22-60 team managed. The offense should climb off the bottom once Markkanen returns and the shooting variance evens out. Neither change turns a lottery team into anything else. The current pace of 8 wins is too low, but this is a high-teens-to-low-20s win team, playing for development and draft position.

strengths.title: A defense that finally holds up
strengths.body: After three years at the bottom, the DRtg has come down to 116.0 from last season's 122.3. The biggest fix is at the rim, where opponents shoot 64.0% against last year's 71.4. Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba have given the frontcourt a C+ grade, the best group on the roster. Ten games is a small sample, but the rim numbers are a big enough swing to treat as largely real.

strengths.title: Finishing possessions on the glass
strengths.body: Utah's 74.5 DRB % ranks 7th, a step up from 72.9 last season. It is one reason opponents' eFG % sits slightly below the league average. Hayes and Bamba are the drivers, and this is the kind of effort-and-size strength that tends to hold.

strengths.title: The young wings are winning minutes
strengths.body: Peterson (+6.8) and Bailey (+7.0) post the best On-Off marks among the heavy-minute players, even on a 1-9 team. Their efficiency is still raw at 51.3 TS % each, but the lineups around them hold up. For a rebuilding team, that matters more than the record.

concerns.title: An offense near the league floor
concerns.body: The 104.4 ORtg ranks 29th, 9 points below the league. It comes from poor shooting (49.5 eFG %, 28th) combined with too many turnovers (15.0 TOV %, 25th). The shooting should regress upward because last year's team made 34.5% of its threes, but the turnover issue predates this season's injuries.

concerns.title: The best scorers are in street clothes
concerns.body: Markkanen is Out after 8 games and Jackson Jr. is Out after only 4, and George is day-to-day. That has pushed bench pieces like Mykhailiuk (33.8 TS %) and Collier into real roles. The scoring slide to 100 points a game over the last five tracks with that thinning roster.

concerns.title: Point guards feast on Utah
concerns.body: Opposing point guards score 33.5 points a game, 28th in the league, and 28.4% of the points against Utah come from PGs. Containing the ball at the point of attack is the weak link in an otherwise improved defense.

trend.note: After a 1-5 October, Utah went 0-4 to open November. The last five games were all losses at a -15.6 differential per game, with scoring down 6.2 points from the season average as the injuries piled up.

weekAhead.headline: Two winnable home games, then Houston and San Antonio.
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with back-to-back home games against Miami (4-6) and Orlando (2-7). Both have defenses ranked 25th and 26th, so they are the softest stops Utah will see for a while. Miami allows a league-worst 58.0 Opp eFG % and gives up heavy scoring to both guard spots. That sets up well for George, if healthy, and Peterson. Orlando's offense is nearly as broken as Utah's, with a 107.9 ORtg. A win in this pair is realistic, and the losing streak should end here if it ends at all.

The back half is much harder. Houston is 7-3 with the 3rd-ranked offense at 119.4 ORtg and A-level wings and frontcourt, and Utah plays them on the road. San Antonio is 8-2 with the 4th-ranked defense and an A+ backcourt, and it has already beaten Utah twice this season. Against a defense that already struggles with point guards, that backcourt is a bad draw. A split of the home pair and two losses after it is the likely outcome.

keyMatchups.title: Utah's guards against Miami's leaky perimeter
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows 31.3 points a game to point guards and 31.6 to shooting guards, and opponents post a 58.0 eFG % against it. It is the best shooting environment Utah will see. If the Jazz offense can't get going here, the problem runs deeper than variance.

keyMatchups.title: Orlando: a matchup of struggling offenses
keyMatchups.body: Orlando's 117.2 DRtg and 15.7 TOV % mirror Utah's own flaws. Its defense gives up 28.78 points a game to power forwards, an opening that fits Markkanen but goes unused while he is Out. Without him, this game comes down to who turns it over less.

keyMatchups.title: San Antonio's guards against Utah's soft spot
keyMatchups.body: The Spurs carry an A+ backcourt into a matchup with a Utah defense that gives up the 28th-most points to point guards. They also allow just 59.4% at the rim, 2nd in the league. That takes away the interior finishing Hayes and Bamba have provided.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the offense can clear its 106.2-point season average against Miami and Orlando's bottom-tier defenses. If it can't, the shooting slump is more than a bad-luck stretch.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 8 wins is too pessimistic. The defense has improved enough to keep this team well clear of last year's 120-plus DRtg range. The shooting is also unlikely to stay at 32.1% from three when last season's group made 34.5%. Markkanen's return would restore the only proven efficient volume scorer, and that alone should lift the offense off 29th. What should hold is the rim protection and defensive rebounding. What should regress upward is the shooting.

The improvements still leave a lottery team. Turnovers are a structural problem, the bench wings have been badly inefficient, and the top of the West is crowded with OKC, Minnesota, Houston and San Antonio. Expect a season in the high teens to low 20s in wins. The real measure will be whether Peterson and Bailey turn their positive On-Off into efficient production.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting regressing toward last year's level

confidence.note: Only ten games, with key scorers missing, so the offense's true level is uncertain. The losing margin and the defensive gains are clear enough to trust.
